facts:
## CELL FACTS

Cell 金_正官 (Metal carrying The Magistrate). Persona The Magistrate (正官). Definition line: "Framework-mediated pressure, the standard that steadies". Keyword Order, charge gentle, poles catalyst Integrity / friction Rigidity. Family function: Order. Cost dimension: the standard that steadies; the frame that holds you holds you in. Arena: the gate, the seal, order, the appointed hour. Classical portrait: framework-mediated pressure; the standard that steadies; rank held by rules, rigidity as the shadow. Ruled domains: Career, Status, Order. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 七杀.
Element arena: Metal (edge, blade, ore, forge, whetstone, the clean line). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Wood. structural_interaction seed: "Metal setting standard for Wood cross-polarity — precision that tests and grants recognition".
- k2_overview: "Your Metal moves as the Magistrate: the law in its own element. Rules read to you like well-machined parts, and you keep them because precision deserves keeping. Rank finds you early, trust follows, and your signature means something. The discipline is real steel. Just check, yearly, that the code you enforce is still one you believe."
- k2_functional: "You are the measure others calibrate to: exact, upright, and honest about your own tolerances."
- adj_chips: {"catalyst":["Precise","Incorruptible","Even-handed"],"friction":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Career":"Your career climbs through correctness: credentials, rank, a record without dents. Institutions promote you because you are what their rules dream of. Pick ones whose rules deserve you.","Status":"Your standing is engraved, earned slowly, hard to tarnish. Guard it without worshiping it. A reputation is a tool for doing right at scale, not the point of the work.","Order":"You produce order like a mint produces coin: standardized, trusted, circulating. Systems you touch stay fixed. Leave a tolerance in every spec. Perfect fits crack under weather."}
- fn_reading.friction.ledger (three rows, index-aligned to adj_chips.friction; authored order is significance order):
  - row 0: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 1: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 2: [REDACTED: the target row]
- Sibling cell 金_七杀 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Battle-ready","Disciplined","Surgical"],"friction":["Punishing","Ruthless","Blunted"]}
- Sibling cell 金_七杀 friction row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Your corrections carry more force than the error weighed. The missed detail gets a review nobody forgets, the small failure gets a consequence with edges, and people leave your feedback sessions altered. Standards were the point once. The punishment developed its own appetite."

Core element Wood, energy element Metal. Law: Metal tames Wood (金克木: the knife prunes the branch). Relative to the core the energy is the tamer, so Metal is this core's Order. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Wood core that shows Metal on the friction pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The friction pole of Metal as the Order is the Underfueled band's case (the core burns more than it takes in); tone by pole: reminder. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 木_金's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: Needing permission comes before wanting, in your order of things. A rule outranks a wish in you, and you wait to be allowed rather than take what is yours. You are the one holding back the permission you keep waiting for.

value_b.text: You need permission for things no rule even covers. The frame that holds you up also holds you in, and you check what is permitted ahead of checking what you want. Know that you need no permission to want.

value.text: Hating being wrong is the part of you that works hardest. A mistake marks your name in your eyes, and you give silence in place of any answer that risks being wrong. You go silent on the answers you had right.

value_b.text: You hate being wrong more than being quiet. Being correct is the nearest you get to safe, and you check an answer three times instead of risking a wrong one. Keep hold of the fact that one wrong answer is cheaper than silence.

value.text: Putting rules first is how you stay steady. A rule asks nothing of your judgement, and you follow it rather than read the person in front of you. Keep this with you, that you hold the rule and the rule does not hold you.

value_b.text: You put rules first because a rule is never disappointed in you. The written rule feels safer than the right call, and you pick it rather than trust your judgement. Remember this much, that you wrote none of the rules and can question one.
